Hypothesis tests: the conclusion mark

Every test ends with one sentence, and it’s worth a mark. Build it — the comparison, the decision, the strength, the context. And never, ever “accept H0”.
Your sentence so far
rounds where all four slots were right on the first check
Where the marks went
Pin this above your desk
Earns the mark
  1. “Since p-value = 0.032 < 0.05” — the comparison, both numbers on the page (or z against the critical region)
  2. “we reject H0” / “we do not reject H0” — the decision
  3. “sufficient / insufficient evidence” — matched to the decision
  4. “at the …% level of significance” — the level, stated every time
  5. “that ⟨claim about the population, in context⟩” — H1’s exact direction, real units
Loses it
✗“accept H0” — you can fail to reject; you can never accept
✗“prove / proven” — a hypothesis test proves nothing; it weighs evidence
Same sentence, every paper. Boring is what full marks looks like.
